summary: Add the independently audited finite-contrast max n=2 norm-orientation and full-Jacobian theorem, then derive exact max n=2 existence and uniqueness by accepted proper continuation, while leaving every general-n and min node unchanged.

node.title: Endpoint-gauge orientation makes every max four-event residual nonsingular
node.statement: For finite R>1 and n=2, the accepted full-relay structure, sharp cell phase theorem, max fixed-mu order, max positive path matrix, parameter-action identity, and exact shape-Hessian identity, together with the independently audited R20 common-terminal determinant package, imply that every max self-consistent point is reflection fixed, has mu>3/2 and c'>0, has a strictly negative shape Hessian, and has nonzero full switch-residual Jacobian.

node.title: Finite-contrast max four-event norm orientation and Jacobian nonsingularity
node.statement: For every finite R>1, every max-law n=2 self-consistent point with exactly four effective switches is reflection invariant and lies in the strict common-terminal chart with mu>3/2. At that point the original equal-norm residual has the positive common-terminal orientation c'>0; equivalently the physical frequency Schur scalar is negative. The complete max shape Hessian is strictly negative definite and the full switch-residual Jacobian is nonsingular. This is restricted to max and n=2 and makes no assertion for n>=3 or the minimum law.

node.title: Proper continuation upgrades max n=2 nonsingularity to uniqueness
node.statement: The established max n=2 full residual-Jacobian nonsingularity eliminates every finite-contrast interior singularity. The accepted properness theorem prevents switch collision or endpoint escape on compact finite-contrast intervals, and accepted small-contrast uniqueness supplies the base component. Therefore the max n=2 self-consistent point exists uniquely for every finite R>1.

node.title: Unique max self-consistent four-event weight at every finite contrast
node.statement: For every finite R>1 there exists exactly one max-self-consistent bang-bang weight with exactly four effective switches (n=2). It is reflection invariant almost everywhere and its ordered switches satisfy x_j+x_(5-j)=1. The theorem does not cover n>=3 or the minimum law and therefore does not settle general O3a.

node.title: Maximum-law four-event endpoint-gauge closure
node.statement: The route closes max n=2 at every finite contrast by combining reflected common-terminal component properness, exact one-end gauge minors, the positive path matrix, and the physical frequency Schur calibration. It remains partial relative to the active all-n max and O3a program: for n>=3 the sole surviving anti-sector endpoint-compensation scalar is still open.
node.method_family: Reflected common-terminal phase chart, exact determinant certificates, boundary-component classification, one-end first-jet gauges, path-matrix congruence, and proper analytic continuation
node.deliverable_contract: A proof or refutation of finite-contrast max n=2 norm orientation, full residual nonsingularity, and uniqueness, with all general-n, min, and degenerate scopes retained explicitly.
falsification_tests: Rebuild the R13 detct certificate and all 1200 exact positive coefficients under the bound interpreter rather than treating common-terminal regularity as a premise.
Classify the collapsed middle cell, both amplitude faces, mu->1 corners, and the legal upper-phase closure before concluding mu>3/2 on every component.
Check that each one-end gauge agrees with the original norm row to first order modulo the same common-terminal constraint; do not reuse the withdrawn R19 two-end ambient partials.
Use the R11 congruence, Schur calibration, and completed-square identity together; local c'>0 alone is not the full switch-Jacobian conclusion.
Do not propagate the n=2 theorem to n>=3, the minimum law, or universal O3a.
node.expected_bottleneck: For max n>=3 the fixed-mu path block is positive, but reflection leaves one physical anti-sector Schur scalar requiring a global endpoint-normalization compensation inequality.

ordered_steps: Use accepted STRUCTURE, FULL-RELAY, and INTERNAL-PHASE-R8 to place every max n=2 self-consistent point in the strict physical four-event common-terminal chart; use MAX-GLOBAL-ORDER-R9 to make it reflection fixed.
Rebuild the hash-bound R13 exact common-terminal certificate, including its 1200 strictly positive coefficients, to prove detct>0 rather than assuming reduced regularity.

For fixed R, use detct>0 to make each common-terminal component a single mu graph. Classify every finite endpoint and simultaneous corner: the collapsed middle cell has mu=3/2, both amplitude faces and mu=1 are impossible, and the legal upper-phase closure has mu>3/2. Hence every interior root has mu>3/2.

Prove the scalar N_L>0 for mu>=3/2. Replace the withdrawn two-end row by separate left and right gauges whose first jets differ from the original norm row only by their own terminal constraint; obtain B1<0<B2 and then detall>0, Omega_2>0, and c'>0 for the original equal-norm residual.

Combine accepted L_+>0 and the parameter-action orientation with the simultaneously audited R11 congruence, frequency Schur calibration, and completed square. Since L'<0 and c'>0, the whole max shape Hessian is strictly negative.
Apply the accepted exact identity H=diag(delta_i)D_xG with every delta_i nonzero at finite R to conclude that the full max n=2 switch-residual Jacobian is nonsingular at every self-consistent point.
boundary_cases: The upper positive-cell phase is retained as a legitimate zero-energy common-terminal closure and shown to have mu>3/2; it is not silently excluded.
The theta->0, mu->1, a->rho, a->1, and coupled amplitude corners are classified before the component argument is used.
R=1, grazing or collided events as interior roots, nontransverse/incomplete words, the minimum law, and n>=3 are outside the local theorem.
R19's two-end ambient-partial claim is withdrawn and is not an input; each one-end gauge is checked at the level of the correct first jet.

ordered_steps: The first R20 inference proves det D_xG_max is nonzero at every finite-contrast max n=2 self-consistent point.

Apply the accepted properness theorem at fixed n=2: the solution set is compact over every finite contrast interval and cannot lose a branch through switch collision or endpoint escape; universal interior nonsingularity therefore makes the count locally constant.
Use accepted small-contrast existence and uniqueness to set this constant count equal to one near R=1, and continue it across all finite R>1.
The accepted properness conclusion also makes the unique point reflection invariant, agreeing with the independent R9 reflection result.
boundary_cases: The conclusion is for every finite R>1 but only n=2 and the maximum law.
No existence, uniqueness, norm orientation, or Jacobian sign is inferred for n>=3 or for the minimum law.
The protected general-n max theorem and the general max norm one-crossing obligation remain unchanged and open.

math_research_state_records.status_justification: The route completely proves the stated max n=2 local and global uniqueness theorems. It remains partial relative to the active all-n max and O3a program because reflection leaves one physical anti-sector endpoint-compensation scalar for n>=3.
